maya: Quick sync — we need to lock decisions for dedicated capacity behavior for Q3 launch: reserved pool semantics, quota expiry, burst shape, and autoscale policy. Can we triage now?
omar: I can drive. Key questions: 1) Do reserved pools permit burst beyond committed baseline? 2) If burst occurs, prefer throttle vs preempt? 3) Billing model for burst (metered vs included)?
lucy: From runtime POV: base = hard reservation. For burst, prefer an elastic buffer that is preemptible with graceful drain hooks. Session stickiness is important — don’t evict an in-flight chat.
ben: SRE data: ran a short sim with 3% tail spikes — unlimited burst -> ~4x p99 latency. Suggest capped burst using per-tenant token buckets + admission control.
ben: Example token-bucket config we tested:
```json
{
  "burst_bucket": {"capacity": 600, "refill_rate_per_min": 60}
}
```
alia: Customer note — several enterprise pilots asked for carryover of unused reserved capacity (e.g., roll 10% unused to next month). They want predictable invoicing and a simple cap. Feels like a sales differentiator but friction for billing.
omar: Proposal draft: - Reserved pools = guaranteed baseline (no preemption). - Burst = token bucket (non-guaranteed, preemptible). - Billing: committed baseline billed monthly; burst metered by minute with a hard ceiling to avoid runaway charges. - Carryover: pilot as a paid add-on (1 month carryover, capped at 10%).
maya: Launch criteria (what we measure before GA): 1) Canary with 3 pilot customers. 2) p50/p95 latency impact in reserve region <10%. 3) No customer-visible error escalations >2 in 30 days. 4) Clear billing docs + contract language. Need commitments from product/eng/sre and signed pilot contracts by June 15.
lucy: Implementation checklist: - routing policy (baseline vs burst lanes) - admission controller changes (token-bucket enforcement) - eviction/handoff hook for in-flight sessions - telemetry labels (tenant/commitment/burst_token) - feature flag to toggle behavior
ben: I'll add quota enforcement to the admission controller and spin the sim job to test edge cases (multi-tenant storms, gradual refill).
sre-bot: sim-job queued: id=5991, config="burst_capacity=600, refill=60/m", expected-run=2026-05-02T14:00:00Z
omar: Decision timeline: we should lock the policy by EOD tomorrow so contracts can align. @lucy can you confirm ETA for the core impl?
lucy: PR ETA: feature flag + admission controller changes by 2026-05-08. Canary rollout ready by 2026-05-15 if sims look good.
maya: Great — I'll draft the customer-facing note + pilot contract terms. @alia please surface top 5 customers for pilot and any billing concerns.
alia: Will do — sending customer list + notes by EOD today.
omar: OK, next steps: 1) ben -> start sim job and share results. 2) lucy -> open feature-flag PR. 3) maya -> draft pilot terms. 4) alia -> customer list. Lock policy tomorrow EOD.
maya: :thumbsup:
ben: started the sim run, will post results as soon as available.
sre-bot: sim-job 5991 started. Logs will be at https://ci.redwood/sims/5991
alia: quick ask — for the carryover pilot: can marketing ship a simple FAQ about limits and billing? we need that before sales pitches.
omar: Yes, I'll coordinate with docs + marketing after policy lock.
lucy: One implementation caveat: if we do per-minute metering for burst, we need fine-grained KV cache tagging to avoid memory leaks. I’ll add that to the ticket.
maya: Thanks all. If anyone has strong objections to the token-bucket + carryover-paid-add-on approach, speak now. Otherwise we’ll lock tomorrow.
omar: No objections from product side.
ben: SRE OK with capped burst. Need to validate thresholds in sim.
lucy: Engineering OK; will push constraints into the admission controller.
alia: customer-facing team aligned.
maya: Closing — will follow up with a short doc and calendar invite for the lock call tomorrow 9am PT.
